text:
Harper Nguyen: dropping a quick thread on a different take for the routing editor compact UX. Problems we're seeing in usability testing: accidental reorders when users try to edit, unclear bulk-fix affordance for matcher errors, and noisy preview recalcs during multi-select changes. Proto: https://figma.com/file/new-compact-pass

Diego Morales: main thing: folks hit the drag handle when they meant to click the rule name to edit. Idea: split handle and inline edit zones with a 12px separator, and add a small 'lock' toggle on the left to temporarily disable drag during edit. :lock:

Keiko Tan: Lock toggle is interesting. If locked, show a thin purple outline and disable drop targets. Tooltip: "Lock to edit: prevents accidental reorder". Should locking persist per-session? I'd vote yes.

Ravi Singh: bulk-fix idea: when multiple rules show the same matcher error, show a top-level banner: "3 rules have the same matcher syntax error. Fix all ->" which opens a mini-editor where you can apply a single corrected expression to selected rules. Saves a lot of clicks in testing.

Tara Bennett: love the bulk-fix. Microcopy for the banner: "Multiple rules share a matcher error. Edit one to apply fix to selected rules." Keep CTA label: "Edit selected". Also ensure undo is obvious: show a toast with "Undo" after apply.

Harper Nguyen: preview behavior: on multi-select reorder or bulk edits, we should snapshot current preview and show a small compare pill: "Preview diff: +4 matches" with a chevron to expand details. Throttle live recalcs to 300ms when multi-editing so we don't DD the backend.

Diego Morales: re: keyboard reorder when locked: allow keyboard users to toggle lock via Space on the lock button. For reorder: Enter to pick up, Ctrl+Arrow to move fast, Enter to drop. Aria-live strings: "Picked up {ruleName}", "Moved to {index} (fast)" for ctrl moves.

Keiko Tan: accessibility: screen reader users need to know a rule is locked. Announce: "Rule {name}, edit-locked". Also for bulk-fix flow, after applying, announce "Applied fix to 3 rules" and read the undo action label. Use polite aria-live.

Ravi Singh: implementation note: bulk-fix should validate the corrected matcher client-side immediately with the matcher parser so users see errors before apply. If the fix fails, show inline hint: "Parser error on line X" and don't allow apply.

Tara Bennett: UI detail: when lock is on, replace the drag cursor with default pointer and add a subtle badge "editing" on the rule. That communicates mode clearly.

DesignBot: automated checks: color contrast OK for purple outline if using `--edit-lock: #6D28D9`, ensure focus ring is 3px and visible in both themes. Keyboard reorder patterns OK if aria-live strings present. Recommend aria-describedby linking for the bulk-fix banner to a hidden summary element.

Harper Nguyen: decisions captured: 1) split handle vs edit zone + 12px separator, 2) add per-session lock toggle with 'editing' badge and purple outline, 3) bulk-fix banner + mini-editor with undo toast and client-side validation, 4) snapshot preview diff pill on multi-edit with 300ms throttle, 5) keyboard affordances including Ctrl+Arrow fast move + aria-live strings, 6) a11y: announce locked state and bulk actions (Keiko to spec). I'll update the figma and create issues under routing-editor epic.

Diego Morales: I'll mock the lock toggle states and cursors.

Keiko Tan: I'll write the aria snippets and accessibility notes for the bulk-fix flow.

Ravi Singh: I'll prototype client-side matcher validation and the mini-editor UX.

Tara Bennett: I'll draft the microcopy for the banner, undo toast, and the preview diff pill. Draft banner copy: "3 rules share a matcher error. Edit one to apply a fix to selected rules." Draft undo toast: "Applied fix to 3 rules. Undo".

Harper Nguyen: timeline: targeting the sprint after next. Please add tickets and tag me. Thanks team! :sparkles:
